For that post, who left the most edit comments, and how many did they leave? Please give me each editor's display name along with their number of edit comments on that post.     SELECT h.UserId, COUNT(DISTINCT h.RevisionGUID) AS edit_comment_count

    WHERE p.Title = 'Why square the difference instead of taking the absolute value in standard deviation?'

failures.question: For each of the SME, LAM, and KAM segments, identify the CZK customer with the lowest total recorded consumption in 2013, breaking a tie by smaller customer ID. What are the differences between those customers' 2013 totals in SME minus LAM, LAM minus KAM, and KAM minus SME order? Round each to two decimals.
failures.answer:
```sql
WITH annual_totals AS (
    SELECT c.Segment, c.CustomerID,
           SUM(CAST(ROUND(y.Consumption * 100) AS INTEGER)) AS total_hundredths
    FROM main.customers AS c
    JOIN main.yearmonth AS y ON y.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
    WHERE c.Currency = 'CZK'
      AND c.Segment IN ('SME', 'LAM', 'KAM')
      AND y.Date BETWEEN '201301' AND '201312'
      AND y.Consumption IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY c.Segment, c.CustomerID
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT annual_totals.*,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
               PARTITION BY Segment ORDER BY total_hundredths, CustomerID
           ) AS segment_rank
    FROM annual_totals
),
winners AS (
    SELECT Segment, CustomerID, total_hundredths
    FROM ranked
    WHERE segment_rank = 1
)
SELECT sme.CustomerID AS sme_customer_id, sme.total_hundredths / 100.0 AS sme_total,
       lam.CustomerID AS lam_customer_id, lam.total_hundredths / 100.0 AS lam_total,
       kam.CustomerID AS kam_customer_id, kam.total_hundredths / 100.0 AS kam_total,
       ROUND((sme.total_hundredths - lam.total_hundredths) / 100.0, 2) AS sme_minus_lam,
       ROUND((lam.total_hundredths - kam.total_hundredths) / 100.0, 2) AS lam_minus_kam,
       ROUND((kam.total_hundredths - sme.total_hundredths) / 100.0, 2) AS kam_minus_sme
FROM winners AS sme
CROSS JOIN winners AS lam
CROSS JOIN winners AS kam
WHERE sme.Segment = 'SME' AND lam.Segment = 'LAM' AND kam.Segment = 'KAM'
LIMIT 1
```

failures.question: For my monthly recap I need the fastest pit stop made during any F1 race held in September 2016. Please tell me the driver's full name, the pit stop time, the name of the race where it happened, the circuit name, and the circuit location. If two or more pit stops share the fastest time, list each of them with its own driver, race, circuit name and circuit location.
failures.answer:
```sql
WITH september_stops AS (
    SELECT p.driverId, p.milliseconds, r.name AS race_name, r.circuitId,
           MIN(p.milliseconds) OVER () AS fastest_ms
    FROM pitStops AS p
    JOIN races AS r ON r.raceId = p.raceId
    WHERE r.date >= '2016-09-01' AND r.date < '2016-10-01'
)
SELECT d.forename || ' ' || d.surname AS driver_name,
       s.milliseconds / 1000.0 AS pit_stop_seconds,
       s.race_name,
       c.name AS circuit_name,
       c.location AS circuit_location
FROM september_stops AS s
JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverId = s.driverId
JOIN circuits AS c ON c.circuitId = s.circuitId
WHERE s.milliseconds = s.fastest_ms
LIMIT -1
```

failures.question: I'm comparing the builds of heroes whose power sets overlap with 3-D Man's. What is the average weight in kg of the heroes other than 3-D Man that share at least one superpower with him? Please round it to two decimal places, leave out any heroes whose weight isn't recorded, and return just that single number.
failures.answer:
```sql
WITH shared_power_heroes AS (
    SELECT candidate.hero_id
    FROM main.superhero AS target
    JOIN main.hero_power AS owned ON owned.hero_id = target.id
    JOIN main.hero_power AS candidate ON candidate.power_id = owned.power_id
    WHERE target.superhero_name = '3-D Man'
      AND candidate.hero_id <> target.id
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(hero.weight_kg), 2) AS average_weight_kg
FROM main.superhero AS hero
WHERE hero.weight_kg IS NOT NULL
  AND hero.id IN (SELECT hero_id FROM shared_power_heroes)
LIMIT 1
```

failures.question: As part of the data-completeness review, I'd like to know how much laboratory follow-up our never-examined patients actually have, split by sex. Could you give me, for each sex (F and M), the average number of laboratory test dates recorded for the patients of that sex who have no examination record at all? Please cover the whole registry, all years, and round the averages to two decimal places. Nothing else needed beyond the two averages.
failures.answer:
```sql
WITH patient_counts AS (
    SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, COUNT(l.Date) AS test_dates
    FROM main.Patient AS p
    LEFT JOIN main.Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID
    WHERE p.SEX IN ('F', 'M')
      AND p.ID NOT IN (
          SELECT e.ID
          FROM main.Examination AS e
          WHERE e.ID IS NOT NULL
      )
    GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN SEX = 'F' THEN test_dates END), 2) AS F,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN SEX = 'M' THEN test_dates END), 2) AS M
FROM patient_counts
LIMIT 1
```
